title: Soil biodiversity supports ecosystem functions
passage: Paraphrase: Soil organisms decompose residues, cycle nutrients, build aggregates, and can help regulate pests and disease. Maintaining diverse soil life is therefore linked to several soil and production functions.

title: Soil biodiversity and food production
passage: Paraphrase: A diverse soil community contributes to decomposition, nutrient availability, water infiltration, and plant health. Management that protects habitat and organic inputs can support these functions together.

title: State of biodiversity for food and agriculture
passage: Paraphrase: Diversity within crops, livestock, managed organisms, and associated wild species provides resilience and ecosystem services. Simplification of production landscapes can increase vulnerability to shocks.

title: Pollinators and agricultural biodiversity
passage: Paraphrase: Pollinating animals are part of agricultural biodiversity and depend on suitable food and nesting resources. Diverse vegetation around fields can support associated biodiversity when local conditions are suitable.

title: Conservation agriculture principles
passage: Paraphrase: Conservation agriculture combines minimum soil disturbance, permanent soil cover, and crop diversification. These principles are intended to protect soil, improve biological processes, and make production more resilient.

title: Soil organic cover and residue management
passage: Paraphrase: Keeping living or dead plant cover on the soil surface helps protect against raindrop impact, evaporation, and temperature extremes. Cover also supplies organic material as it decomposes.

title: Soil disturbance and conservation agriculture
passage: Paraphrase: Reducing soil disturbance can protect soil structure and organisms, but equipment, weed pressure, residue conditions, and local soils affect the result. Transition should be adapted to farm constraints.

title: Crop diversification in conservation agriculture
passage: Paraphrase: Rotations and associations of crops interrupt pest and disease cycles, diversify residues, and can improve use of water and nutrients. Compatible crop choices depend on climate, markets, and farm equipment.

title: Cover crops for soil health
source_locator: Cover crops for soil health, benefits
passage: Paraphrase: Cover crops can reduce erosion, improve aggregate stability, increase soil organic matter over time, and provide living roots between cash crops. Species and termination timing should match the production system.

title: Soil health assessment principles
passage: Paraphrase: Soil health is assessed through physical, chemical, and biological indicators rather than one measurement. Monitoring should connect management changes to indicators such as aggregation, infiltration, organic matter, and biological activity.

title: Nutrient management and soil testing
passage: Paraphrase: Nutrient decisions should use field information and soil or plant tests, then match nutrient sources and timing to crop demand. This reduces avoidable losses while maintaining crop nutrition.

title: Soil carbon and organic amendments
passage: Paraphrase: Organic matter supports aggregation, water-holding capacity, nutrient supply, and biological habitat. Inputs such as residues, roots, and suitable amendments should be planned with local nutrient and contamination risks.

title: Erosion and soil conservation
passage: Paraphrase: Wind and water erosion remove productive topsoil and can transport sediment and attached nutrients. Vegetative cover, contour practices, and reduced disturbance are common control tools selected for site conditions.

title: Riparian forest buffers
passage: Paraphrase: Vegetated riparian areas can slow runoff, stabilize stream banks, provide habitat, and filter some sediment and nutrients before they reach water. Width and species should reflect site objectives and local guidance.

title: Pollinator habitat conservation
passage: Paraphrase: Pollinator habitat planning considers seasonal flowers, nesting resources, pesticide exposure, and connectivity. Local native plants and management timing should be selected for the target pollinator community.

title: Agroforestry and conservation benefits
passage: Paraphrase: Agroforestry places trees or shrubs with crops, livestock, or water features to address goals such as wind protection, habitat, runoff reduction, and diversified production. Designs must account for competition and management access.

title: Climate change and land: soil management
source_locator: Special Report on Climate Change and Land, summary for policymakers
passage: Paraphrase: Land management can reduce degradation and build resilience, while climate impacts interact with water availability, soil condition, and biodiversity. Context-specific adaptation is needed because practices have trade-offs.

title: Climate change and land: land degradation
source_locator: Special Report on Climate Change and Land, chapter 4
passage: Paraphrase: Erosion, vegetation loss, and declining soil quality can reinforce one another. Measures that retain cover, improve soil organic matter, and manage water can reduce several degradation pathways when appropriately implemented.

title: Water management and climate resilience
source_locator: Special Report on Climate Change and Land, chapter 7
passage: Paraphrase: Improved water management, soil moisture conservation, and diversified systems can contribute to adaptation, but water interventions need to consider downstream users and local hydrology.

title: Biodiversity and ecosystem services
source_locator: Global assessment report, summary for policymakers
passage: Paraphrase: Biodiversity underpins ecosystem functions and contributions such as pollination, pest regulation, soil formation, and water regulation. Responses are more durable when they address habitat, pressures, and local livelihoods together.

title: Drivers of biodiversity decline
passage: Paraphrase: Land-use change, direct exploitation, pollution, invasive species, and climate change are major interacting pressures on biodiversity. Action planning should identify which pressures are active at the site.

title: Ecological connectivity
source_locator: Global assessment report, responses and connectivity
passage: Paraphrase: Connected and well-managed habitat can support movement and ecological processes, while fragmentation reduces options for many species. Corridors should be designed around target species and the surrounding land uses.

title: Integrated pest management
passage: Paraphrase: Integrated pest management considers available pest-control techniques and combines biological, chemical, physical, and cultural measures to suppress pests while minimizing pesticide use and associated risks.

title: Pollination services for sustainable agriculture
source_locator: Global Action on Pollination Services for Sustainable Agriculture
passage: Paraphrase: Pollinators support crop production and biodiversity, and monitoring pollinator declines and interactions helps guide management. Habitat and pesticide decisions should account for pollinator needs and local crop context.

title: Global assessment of soil pollution
source_locator: Global assessment of soil pollution, summary
passage: Paraphrase: Soil pollution can impair soil functions and expose people and ecosystems through food, dust, and water pathways. Assessment should identify contaminants, sources, pathways, and land-use receptors before selecting remediation.

title: Soil pollution prevention and management
source_locator: Global assessment of soil pollution, response options
passage: Paraphrase: Prevention and source control are preferred where possible, while management decisions should be based on contaminant-specific testing and risk assessment. Land use may need to change when exposure cannot be controlled.

title: Land restoration for achieving the SDGs
source_locator: IRP report summary and land restoration chapter
passage: Paraphrase: Land restoration and rehabilitation support land stewardship and can contribute to multiple sustainable-development outcomes. Planning should link restoration actions to measurable land and ecosystem indicators.

title: Ecosystem restoration principles
source_locator: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration principles
passage: Paraphrase: Restoration should be locally appropriate, inclusive, and sustained over time. Reference ecosystems, pressures, recovery indicators, and maintenance needs should be defined before claiming success.

title: Soil moisture conservation
passage: Paraphrase: Surface residues and living cover reduce direct soil exposure and can conserve water by reducing evaporation. The outcome depends on residue amount, climate, soil, and competition with the crop.

title: Rainfed agriculture and water management
source_locator: Rainfed agriculture and agricultural water management overview
passage: Paraphrase: Rainfed agriculture depends on matching crops and management practices to local rainfall patterns and soil-water conditions. Monitoring seasonal water availability helps choose feasible soil-cover and water-conservation actions without assuming one practice fits every farm.

title: Agroecology and diversified systems
passage: Paraphrase: Agroecological approaches use ecological processes and interactions to reduce external pressure and build resilient food systems. Diversification, recycling, efficiency, and synergies are context-dependent design principles.

title: Habitat restoration and native plants
source_locator: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration, principles
passage: Paraphrase: Restoration planning should use locally suitable species and address the causes of degradation. Native plant communities can provide habitat, but establishment and long-term management determine whether benefits persist.

title: Biodiversity indicators for land management
passage: Paraphrase: Biodiversity status and trends can be described using multiple indicators, and no single indicator captures all dimensions. Indicator choice should match the management objective and the species or functions of concern.

title: Soil carbon monitoring
source_locator: Special Report on Climate Change and Land, soil carbon
passage: Paraphrase: Soil carbon responses vary with climate, soil, land use, and management history. Claims about changes should use consistent sampling and account for uncertainty and depth rather than relying on short-term visual impressions.

title: Sustainable land management trade-offs
source_locator: Special Report on Climate Change and Land, trade-offs
passage: Paraphrase: Land interventions can produce benefits in one objective while creating costs or trade-offs in another. Planning should state the target outcomes, local constraints, and indicators used to check unintended effects.

title: Managing invasive alien species
source_locator: Assessment report on invasive alien species, summary
passage: Paraphrase: Invasive alien species can alter ecosystem functions and reduce native biodiversity. Prevention, early detection, containment, and context-specific control are complementary management options.

title: Water quality for ecosystem and human health
source_locator: Water Quality for Ecosystem and Human Health, 2nd edition
passage: Paraphrase: Water-quality monitoring and assessment help identify pressures and guide responses for ecosystems and people. Agricultural runoff and pollutant pathways should be measured and addressed at the relevant catchment scale.

title: Adaptive management and evidence
passage: Paraphrase: Management should be adapted through observation, measurement, learning, and adjustment. A practical plan pairs actions with indicators and a review point so that interventions can be corrected when results differ from expectations.

title: Soil pH measurement and interpretation
source_locator: Soil pH technical note, measurement and interpretation sections (May 2014)
passage: Paraphrase: Soil pH is a chemical indicator whose interpretation depends on soil properties and management history. A measured pH should be considered with texture, organic matter, and fertilizer or amendment history rather than used alone to prescribe a rate.

title: Sustainable forest management and biodiversity
source_locator: Sustainable forest management and biodiversity overview
passage: Paraphrase: Forest management choices influence habitat condition, biodiversity, and the pressures associated with forest loss. Monitoring land-use change and retaining or restoring suitable habitat can help address deforestation-related biodiversity risk.

title: Climate interactions with land and water
source_locator: Special Report on Climate Change and Land, climate and land interactions
passage: Paraphrase: Temperature and precipitation patterns interact with soil condition, water availability, land use, and biodiversity. Climate descriptors should therefore be combined with local soil and water observations when selecting adaptation measures.
